subject: Dedicated capacity pricing for Acero Health — sizing & SLA
body:
From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acerohealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing for Acero Health — sizing + SLA

Hi Olga,

We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a primary inference tier (clinical decision-support pipelines). High level profile:
- Steady-state requests: ~35–55 requests/sec (peak 70s)
- Average context size: 2.5k tokens in, 400 tokens out
- Typical concurrency: 120 concurrent users producing parallel requests in bursts
- Workload mix: 65% short completion, 35% long-context (5–10s gen)

We need: throughput assurance (p99 latency targets), predictable monthly cost, and a 12–24 month reserved commit. Can you share sizing guidance (GPU pool recommendation), pricing tiers, and what discount levels are available for a 12–18 month commit? Also any suggested autoscale/burst strategy?

Thanks — appreciate a ballpark so we can review internally.

— Liam
Liam O'Neal
Director, Platform Engineering
Acero Health

----

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acerohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:05 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing for Acero Health — sizing + SLA

Hi Liam — thanks for the detail, this is helpful. I pulled together a quick estimate and a few options for how to approach a reserved pool that meets p99 latency and gives headroom for bursts. See summary below — I'll attach the options spreadsheet for numbers.

Short summary (ballpark):
- Recommended starting GPU pool: 8x A100s (or equivalent) with continuous batching and 2x burst nodes to cover peak 70 r/s with 120 concurrent short-lived connections.
- Expected baseline throughput: ~50 r/s sustained at p95 < 120ms token latency depending on model; p99 latency depends on model variant — we include SLO credits if p99 exceeds target.
- Commit options: 12-month reserved: 20% uplift over hourly (with 10–15% discount available for committed monthly payment) — 18-month: additional 5% on top of that in some cases.
- Autoscale: keep a small warm pool and enable burst nodes billed at lower reserved discount.

Two asks before finalizing: 1) which model family (+ quantization level) you'll serve, 2) the monthly request distribution (hourly profile) if available.

I'm attaching 'acero_pricing_options_v2.xlsx' with three scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive) and a short draft MOP (method of procedure) describing failover and burst handling.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Attachments: acero_pricing_options_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), acero_draft_mop_v1.pdf (doc)

----

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:32 -0400
Subject: INTERNAL: Acero — draft pricing options & ask for guidance on discounting

Team — forwarding the Acero profile. I drafted three packaging options in the spreadsheet attached to share with the customer. Key constraints: they want predictable monthly costs, p99 targets, and a 12–18 month reserved commit.

My draft recommendations (short):
- Option A (Conservative): 10 A100-equivalent GPUs. Targets: sustained 55 r/s, 2x burst nodes for 75 r/s peak. Price: list reserve rate + standard 15% commit discount. Good if they want margin for growth.
- Option B (Balanced): 8 GPUs. Targets: sustained 45–50 r/s, 2x burst nodes for 70 r/s. Price: list reserve rate with 20% commit discount for 12-month prepay; 23% for 18-month prepay.
- Option C (Aggressive): 6 GPUs. Targets: sustained 30–40 r/s with aggressive scheduling and cache tuning. Price: list reserve rate with 12% discount.

Notes:
- The model family matters a lot; if they use a 2x larger context encoder we'll recommend +2 GPUs.
- p99 guarantees should be paired with reasonable token-rate SLOs. If they want tight p99 (e.g., <300ms for long contexts) we'll add a p99 protection buffer (extra 1–2 GPUs) and SLA credit structure.

Requesting: 1) Marcus — do you see risk on pricing bands vs target margin? 2) Ben — can we push a 20% floor on 12-month and 25% for 18-month when prepay? 3) Marissa — is the MOP wording for failover/lossy fallback acceptable for a HIPAA-ish workload?

Cheers,
Olga

----

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:15 -0400
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Acero — draft pricing options & ask for guidance on discounting

+1 to Option B as the conversational sweet spot. A few commercial notes:
- If they prepay 12 months upfront we can do 22% discount (margin still OK because they'll be steady). For 18 months prepaid we can comfortably land at 27% with legal approval.
- Offer: include 2 months of burst credits (to handle onboarding spikes) and an SLA appendix that defines p99 per-model class with 12% service credit per missed month.
- Ask procurement to sign the standard MOP appendix; we should avoid long-term custom MOPs in the first contract.

I'll prepare a tidy one-pager and a DocuSign link with the 12-mo prepaid Option B at 22% and the 18-mo at 27%.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: (internal) pricing_calc_notes.xlsx

----

From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acerohealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:47 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing for Acero Health — sizing + SLA

Olga — thanks, the spreadsheet helped. We're leaning to Option B but want to confirm two items before we proceed:
1) Can you move the 12-month prepaid discount from 22% to 25% if we commit to an annual review and a 6-month lookback usage clause?
2) We'd prefer the pool sized for a little extra headroom — would you accept 9 GPUs (instead of 8) and keep pricing at the 12-month prepaid level (adjusted discount above)?

We also need the SLA appendix to explicitly call out p99 for the long-context path (we target <750ms) and an emergency rollback path if a model change causes regressions.

If we can get the 25% for 12 months + 9 GPUs with 2 months burst credits, we'll get procurement to sign within the week.

— Liam

----

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acerohealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:02 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing for Acero Health — sizing + SLA

Liam — appreciate the clarity, and happy to move quickly. Confirming final terms we can commit to:

1) Pool sizing: 9x A100-equivalent GPUs (warm pool + 2 burst nodes included).
2) Pricing: 12-month prepaid reserved commit at 25% discount (we'll route through commercial approval but Ben has clearance to present this to procurement).
3) Onboarding credits: 2 months of burst credits (applied to the first two billing cycles).
4) SLA: p99 appendix will specify model-class p99 targets; for their long-context path we will target <750ms p99. If monthly p99 misses exceed the threshold, service credits equal to 12% of that month's dedicated subscription will apply.
5) Safety: emergency rollback + canary rollout wording will be added to the MOP appendix.

Next steps: I'll attach the updated pricing sheet and a one-pager. Ben will send the DocuSign with these terms (link included). Once procurement signs we'll set a kickoff and run a capacity validation (two-week soak + load test).

Attachments: acero_pricing_options_v2.xlsx (updated — includes 9 GPU row), docusign_acero_347_link.txt

Thanks — we'll aim to have the DocuSign by EOD.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

-----

- acero_pricing_options_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet; scenarios: conservative/balanced/aggressive; includes cost breakouts, CPU/GPU headroom assumptions)
- acero_draft_mop_v1.pdf (short MOP describing canary, rollback, monitoring hooks)
- docusign_acero_347_link.txt (DocuSign: https://docusign.net/XYZ-ACERO-347)

[Internal notes]
- Sales: follow up on procurement timeline and payment method (PO vs prepay).
- Solutions: schedule capacity validation run — recommend 48hr trace replay + 2-week soak.
